jurors.top_concern: Primary CTA lacks visual weight; hierarchy is flat.

answers.primary_action_first_glance: Eye lands on the 'HeardRight' logo and 'Legal' text first due to size/weight, not the primary action.
answers.choice_overload: Low. Only 2 main options (Get Started / Contact) and 3 feature links. Good focus.
answers.wcag_violations: Likely contrast failure on the 'Get Started' button if it is light gray on white; touch targets for nav links appear <36px.
answers.microcopy_pull: Button: 'Get Started'. Rewrite: 'Start Free Trial' or 'Create Account' for specificity.
answers.peak_and_end: Peak is the clean feature list; End is the footer. No strong emotional peak designed.
answers.intention_alternative_path: User wants legal protection. A simple 'Download Policy' link might suffice vs. a full dashboard.

blockers.text: Increase visual weight of the primary CTA (Get Started) using a brand color or high-contrast background to establish hierarchy.
Ensure touch targets for top navigation links meet 36x36px minimum for mobile usability.
Verify color contrast ratio of the primary CTA and body text meets WCAG 2.1 AA 4.5:1.
Add a focus ring style to interactive elements for keyboard navigation visibility.

jurors.top_concern: Primary CTA 'Get Started' is buried in a top-right utility bar with no visual weight, while the hero offers no clear next action — Hick's Law violation at the most critical moment.

answers.primary_action_first_glance: Eye lands on the centered wordmark 'HeardRight' inside the soft blue circle. The actual primary CTA 'Get Started' sits in the top-right utility nav with low contrast and small size — competing with 'Sign In' rather than dominating. NNG violation: utility beats action.
answers.choice_overload: Top nav exposes 4 items (Product, Solutions, Pricing, Resources) plus Sign In + Get Started = 6 decisions before any value is communicated. For a landing hero this is high Hick's cost. Defer Pricing/Resources to footer or hamburger.
answers.wcag_violations: (1) 'Get Started' button text on light-blue background likely fails 4.5:1 — appears ~3:1. (2) No visible focus ring on any interactive element. (3) Top-nav hit targets look ~32px tall, below 44px mobile guideline. (4) Hero subhead gray-on-white may sit near 3.5:1.
answers.microcopy_pull: Generic: 'Get Started' — rewrite to outcome-led: 'See your first compliance report →' or 'Run a free 14-day audit'. Also 'Sign In' is fine but 'Learn More' (if present) should be replaced with specific value.
answers.peak_and_end: Peak moment is undesigned — the hero shows a logo + tagline but no proof, demo, or emotional payoff (no testimonial, no stat, no product visual). End moment dumps user at a form/CTA with no preceding trust build. Peak-End rule fails on both ends.
answers.most_concrete_visible_defect: The 'Get Started' button in the top-right has insufficient contrast against its light-blue pill background (text appears pale, ~3:1 ratio) and is visually outweighed by the large centered logo — the primary conversion action is the least prominent element on screen.

blockers.text: Promote the primary CTA: move 'Get Started' into the hero as a high-contrast solid button (dark text on white or white on brand-blue, ≥4.5:1), 48px tall, with a specific outcome label — not a generic verb. The top-right utility slot should hold only Sign In.
Fix contrast on the existing 'Get Started' pill: current pale-on-pale fails WCAG 2.1 AA. Use brand-blue fill with white text, or dark navy text on white fill. Verify with contrast checker ≥4.5:1.
Add a visible focus ring (2px solid, ≥3:1 against adjacent colors) to every nav link and button — currently no keyboard-focus affordance is rendered.
Reduce top-nav choice load: collapse Product/Solutions/Pricing/Resources into a single 'Platform' menu + Pricing link. Apply Hick's Law — fewer paths before the hero CTA.

Design the peak moment: add a product visual, a single bold stat (e.g., 'Trusted by 2,400+ legal teams'), or a short testimonial under the hero headline. The current hero is empty whitespace + logo — no emotional payoff.

Rewrite hero microcopy: replace generic tagline with outcome-specific line (e.g., 'Automated compliance evidence collection, audit-ready in 48 hours'). Add a secondary text link 'See how it works' for non-ready visitors.
Increase mobile hit targets: top-nav items render ~32px tall — bump to ≥44px and ensure the hamburger collapses 4+ items on <768px viewports.

Add brand-token consistency check: the soft blue circle, navy text, and gray subhead should map to named CSS tokens (--brand-primary, --text-primary, --text-muted) — currently the palette feels ad-hoc.

jurors.top_concern: Primary CTA lacks visual dominance; secondary nav and decorative elements compete for attention, violating Hick's Law and reducing conversion clarity.

answers.primary_action_first_glance: Eye lands on the hero image or headline, not the CTA. The 'Get Started' button blends with the background due to low contrast and lack of shadow/elevation, failing to guide the user immediately.
answers.choice_overload: Top nav has 5+ items plus a login button. Consider collapsing secondary links into a dropdown or hamburger menu to reduce cognitive load and focus on the primary conversion path.
answers.wcag_violations: The primary CTA button text likely fails 4.5:1 contrast ratio against the light background. Focus rings are not visible in the static mockup, risking keyboard navigation failure.
answers.microcopy_pull: Current: 'Get Started'. Rewrite: 'Start Your Free Case Review' — adds value proposition and reduces ambiguity about the next step.
answers.peak_and_end: Peak is the hero headline, but it’s not emotionally resonant. End is a generic footer. The journey lacks a clear 'win' state or reassurance after the CTA click.
answers.largest_visual_comprehension_cost: Users must scan the entire hero section to find the CTA because it doesn’t visually pop. The decorative background pattern distracts from the action, increasing time-to-understand.

blockers.text: Increase CTA contrast and add elevation (shadow/border) to make it the most prominent element. Ensure WCAG AA compliance for button text.
Simplify top navigation. Move secondary links to a dropdown or footer to reduce choice overload and focus on the primary conversion goal.
Add visible focus rings to all interactive elements for keyboard accessibility. Test with Tab navigation to ensure logical order.
Rewrite CTA microcopy to include value proposition (e.g., 'Start Your Free Case Review') to reduce ambiguity and increase click-through.
Reduce decorative background pattern opacity or remove it to prevent visual noise from competing with the primary content and CTA.
